pairs.difference: A: grey steel pan with small gold nuggets on green rays. The neutral hero sets off the green backdrop, though the pan's shadow side picks up green in the lens. B: the brass lamp is a strong copper-orange and the glass chimney is lit yellow-green, sitting on yellow-green rays. Hero and backdrop come from neighbouring warm-yellow hues, so the lamp blends into the backdrop instead of standing against it.
pairs.fix: Make the lamp base a dull, aged brass with brown-grey shadows. Keep the glass chimney clear and slightly cool grey, not tinted green-yellow. Set it against a cooler, bluer-green backdrop.

pairs.difference: A: silver harmonica with blue end caps on hot-pink waves. The hero is mostly neutral metal with one blue accent. B: the fan's paper is pure, fully saturated violet across every panel, with no muted step between the lit and shadow panels. The handle turns salmon-pink in the lens. Its subject chroma (0.226) is above every real card.
pairs.fix: Paint the fan paper as a softer lilac-purple. Shadow folds go deeper and slightly bluer, not just brighter violet. The bamboo ribs stay a muted tan.

pairs.difference: A: brown felt hat with one red band on cool blue rays. This is the real warm-hero-on-cool-backdrop setup, and the hat's shadows stay rich red-brown. B: the scout jacket's dark green sash repeats the green ray backdrop exactly, and the orange collar and cuffs add a second loud warm. The tan body reads greenish in the lens, so the hero and backdrop share a hue.
pairs.fix: Change the sash to a deep red or navy so no part of the jacket matches the backdrop. Or put the jacket on a cool blue backdrop. Make the collar and cuffs a muted brown leather instead of bright orange.

pairs.difference: A: orange-red pump on orange desert sand, with red mesas and a peach-lilac sunset sky. The whole card is pulled warm (warm share 0.80, above the real range), and the red pump repeats the red of the mesas. B: red buoy and gold bell on a cool blue sea and sky, a clean warm-hero/cool-backdrop split with purple-maroon shadows.
pairs.fix: Put the red pump against a cool blue-sky backdrop with pale grey-blue distant mesas. Drop the orange glow from the ground so only the pump carries the warm red.

pairs.difference: A: red-and-white popcorn cart with gold trim on a blue diamond backdrop over pale cobbles. Shadows on the red body go deep maroon, and the cobbles give the eye a neutral rest area. B: brown saddle on a hay bale whose strands are pushed to pure yellow-orange across a large area. The saddle's shadows stay the same orange-brown as its lit side, and the cyan backdrop is very loud.
pairs.fix: Paint the hay bale as a pale, dusty straw colour with grey-brown shadows between the strands. Make the saddle's shadow side go toward a deep plum-brown, and soften the cyan backdrop to a calmer blue.

pairs.difference: A: the rocking chair is pure saturated orange wood with a pure lime-green cushion, on a royal-blue stripe wall over yellow-orange floorboards. Its shadows stay the same orange, darkened, and no neutral area rests the eye. B: an orange barrel with grey metal hoops on a dirt floor. The hoops give a neutral break, though the barrel repeats the floor's hue.
pairs.fix: Paint the chair in a natural honey-brown wood with darker brown, slightly violet shadows. Make the cushion a muted sage or dusty red instead of lime. Use a paler, greyer floor so it does not echo the chair.

pairs.difference: A: brown leather boots with one teal stitch accent on a violet backdrop, with maroon-purple shadows related to the backdrop. B: blue sneakers carry neon green, teal, pink, orange and white accents at once (5.5 hue families, above the real range), on an orange wall and a cream floor. Too many accents compete, with no single accent role.
pairs.fix: Keep the sneakers blue with white soles and one accent colour only, for example lime laces. Remove the pink and orange sole bits, and put them on a single cool or muted backdrop.

pairs.difference: A: green cactus with one pink flower accent on yellow rays and sand. The shadows go olive. B: yellow duck with an orange beak, red handles and a blue base on green rays. The duck's shadows and the sand shadow both go red-orange, and it piles up three pure primaries on the toy.
pairs.fix: Let the duck's shadows go toward a soft olive-brown instead of red-orange. Limit the toy to yellow plus one accent: make the handles the same blue as the base. Give the sand a cooler shadow.

pairs.difference: A: beige stone fountain with cyan water on yellow stripes. The stone reads near-neutral grey-green in the lens, and the water is the single cool accent. B: the wagon's canvas is warm cream and its shadow side turns olive-yellow. The wheel rims are pure saturated red, and the brown wood repeats the orange dirt floor, so everything below the canvas is one warm family.
pairs.fix: Paint the canvas cover as a cooler off-white with blue-grey shadows. Make the wheel rims a muted brick red, and use a paler, greyer dirt ground so the wooden wagon body separates from it.

pairs.difference: B is the real lighthouse from the lessons: cool grey-white bricks and clouds, with dark maroon-red shadows. A: the windmill's clouds turn cream-beige in the lens, the same warm-white drift as the generated lighthouses. The ground, grass and tower are all orange-gold, and the blades are only lightly cool.
pairs.fix: Paint the clouds pure white with blue-grey shadows. Make the dry grass a paler, desaturated straw, and give the metal blades a clear cool grey-blue.

pairs.difference: A: campfire scene where the fire, logs, rocks, kettle, cabin window and ground all go orange-tan. Shadows lose colour into flat brown (shadow chroma kept 0.57, below the real range), and pure green grass tufts and a navy sky add more hue families. B: blue viewer on a pale blue city. It is near-monochrome cool, but the shadows keep a related deeper blue.
pairs.fix: Let the rocks and kettle stay cool grey with blue-violet shadows from the night sky, and keep the orange light to the fire and the faces nearest it. Mute the grass tufts to a dark blue-green.

pairs.difference: A: the neck pillow is one pure, fully saturated royal blue, with a shadow that only steps to deeper ultramarine. Subject chroma 0.19 is at the top of the real range, and the pink ring backdrop is equally loud, so hero and backdrop compete. B: blue bottle with a cyan translucent mix on yellow-orange rays. The hero is less pure, and some light comes through it.
pairs.fix: Paint the pillow as a softer, slightly greyed denim blue with gentle navy-violet shadows. Make the pink backdrop paler and calmer so the pillow is the louder of the two.

pattern: Generated cards push the hero to one pure, fully saturated hue, like the orange glove, violet fan, lime cushion or royal-blue pillow. Their shadows only darken the same hue (orange-brown or red-orange) instead of shifting to the cool violet, maroon or plum seen in the real cards. Whites and clouds drift warm cream instead of cool grey. The whole card gets pulled warm, or the hero repeats a backdrop hue. Several pure accents compete where real cards use one.
